subject: CedarBank security notice — request to preserve logs and IRP details
messages:
From: Elena Torres <elena.torres@cedarbank.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, security@redwood.com
Cc: Andrew Mills <andrew.mills@cedarbank-legal.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Suspected exfiltration — please preserve logs and engage IRP

Hi Vivek,

We detected anomalous S3 GET activity originating from an IP range that appears to have accessed a small set of objects in a CedarBank test bucket that contains customer PII derivatives. At this point we are treating this as a potential data exfiltration event.

What we need immediately:
- Confirmation you will preserve all relevant logs (API gateway, S3 access logs, instance console logs, auth events) for 90 days.
- An intake path for us to transfer artifacts (preferred: SFTP with signed PGP or secure Share link).
- Point of contact for IR communications and an initial timeline for Redwood's investigation.

We have preserved our side and initiated our internal incident response. Please treat this with high priority — our compliance team is included (Andrew Mills).

Attachments: cedarbank_initial_notify.msg (email export)

Thanks,
Elena Torres
Head of Security Operations
CedarBank
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Elena Torres <elena.torres@cedarbank.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 09:38:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Suspected exfiltration — please preserve logs and engage IRP

Elena — thanks for the heads-up and sorry you're seeing this. We are treating this as priority incident. Confirming the following immediate actions: 

1) Preservation: We will preserve all candidate telemetry (s3 access logs, object manifests, control-plane audit logs, instance console and kube audit) for 90 days and take snapshots of affected instances.
2) Intake: We can accept evidence via SFTP (preferred) or an encrypted Drive share. I'll have Marissa (Security Ops) provide SFTP credentials and ingestion instructions.
3) Point of contact: I'm leading the customer communication; Marissa will run ingestion/forensics and Jonas will provide the timeline and technical analysis. Lauren is on legal and will coordinate with Andrew on evidence handling & any subpoena/retention constraints.

Next steps I will take now: start a targeted KV-cache and prefix-cache freeze on the affected model endpoints (to avoid additional exposure), request immediate token rotation for service accounts that showed activity, and begin retaining request traces.

I will follow up with a play-by-play and an SFTP endpoint within the hour.

— Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Reliability & Security
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Elena Torres <elena.torres@cedarbank.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, jonas_weber@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Suspected exfiltration — evidence intake details

Elena — sending the intake path and instructions. Apologies for the brief message; coordinating with forensics now.

SFTP endpoint: sftp.redwood-secure.com (user: cedarbank_incident_9843)
Auth: public-key only (please email PGP-signed pubkey to secure@redwood.com)
Retention: Files will be kept in an isolated bucket for 90 days by default; we will not alter object ACLs.
Required manifest: evidence_index_20261120.csv (CSV with filename, MD5, timestamp, brief description).
Contact: marissa_cole@redwood.com (ops), jonas_weber@redwood.com (forensics)

Attached: redwood_preserve_instructions.pdf (guidance on minimal data we need + PGP instructions).

If you prefer a direct transfer, we can provide a one-time pre-signed S3 target — let me know.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Security Operations Manager
Redwood Inference
From: Elena Torres <elena.torres@cedarbank.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Andrew Mills <andrew.mills@cedarbank-legal.com>, security@cedarbank.com
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 08:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Suspected exfiltration — evidence transfer completed

Marissa / Vivek — we've uploaded the initial artifact bundle to the SFTP you provided. Contents: auth-logs.tar.gz (contains timestamped auth events, redacted where necessary), s3-manifest.csv, sample payloads (scrubbed). The SFTP user is cedarbank_incident_9843; transfer completed at 2026-11-18T07:55:00-08:00 UTC.

We also included a brief internal timeline:
- 2026-11-15 22:40 UTC: anomalous GETs observed against test-bucket-cedar-eu
- 2026-11-15 23:10 UTC: internal triage flagged unusual IP range and escalated to SOC

Please confirm receipt and that the preserved artifacts are accessible. We're also happy to provide a redacted sample of the payloads if that helps your analysis.

Thanks,
Elena
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Elena Torres <elena.torres@cedarbank.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 11:18:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Suspected exfiltration — initial timeline and findings

Elena — confirmed, I was able to pull the uploaded bundle and start correlation with our ingress/egress traces. Initial notes (high level):

- Scope: activity tied to a compromised API key used by a legacy ingestion job (readonly key) that permitted GET on a subset of test objects. No evidence of write/delete operations.
- Duration: ~16 minutes of intermittent access (see attached evidence_index_20261120.csv for object-level timestamps).
- Exposure: appears limited to test fixtures; we have not yet identified production PII exfiltration.
- Actions taken: rotated the implicated service key, revoked pre-signed token cache, enabled additional request tracing and snapshot of affected nodes.

I've staged our artifacts here for your download: https://drive.redwood.com/s/cedarbank-evidence (access granted to cedarbank_incident_9843).

I'll produce a full technical write-up and timeline by Monday; in the meantime, please let us know if CedarBank wants an independent third-party forensic review — we can suggest partners and coordinate.

— Jonas
Principal Forensics Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Elena Torres <elena.torres@cedarbank.com>, Andrew Mills <andrew.mills@cedarbank-legal.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 15:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Redwood post-incident summary and next steps

Elena / Andrew — attaching our post-incident summary and remediation plan. High-level summary:

- Root cause: compromised legacy ingestion API key with excessive read scope; attacker accessed a small set of test fixtures.
- Impact: no confirmed production-customer PII accessed; limited to test dataset containing derivative PII.
- Remediation performed: API key rotation (completed 2026-11-16T09:42), isolated evidence bucket with 90-day retention, augmentation of request logging, enforcement of least-privilege on legacy keys, and rollout of warning automation to detect abnormal GET rate patterns.
- Outstanding: agreed joint review of key lifecycle practices and expiration policy; suggested third-party forensic audit (if CedarBank requests).

Attachments: redwood_postmortem_20261123.pdf (detailed timeline, artifact index, action items).
Action owners: Jonas (forensic write-up, due 2026-11-29), Marissa (SFTP retention & access audit, due 2026-11-30), Lauren & Andrew (legal evidence handling confirmation, due 2026-11-27).

Please confirm acceptance of the postmortem and whether CedarBank requires any additional artifacts or a formal SOC2 SIG crosswalk for your records.

Best,
Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Reliability & Security
Redwood Inference
